page: Microsoft Azure E48bs_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance engineered for memory-intensive workloads that demand high remote block storage throughput. It is powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 48 virtual CPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, backed by support for instruction sets including AVX-512, VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Memory capacity is provisioned at 384.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. In synthetic throughput benchmarks, the memory subsystem demonstrates strong uncached large-block performance, achieving 259.6 GB/sec in read bandwidth and 128.15 GB/sec in write bandwidth. The instance does not bundle any local storage, relying entirely on Azure remote managed disks with Premium Storage and enhanced block storage performance capabilities. It does not include hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight solid compute and memory metrics. The platform records strong performance in PassMark database operations (23,477.08), PassMark overall CPU score (50,828.28), PassMark memory score (2,814.85), and encryption tests (43,888.77). Static web serving throughput also achieves strong marks at 45.29 GB/sec. General multi-core processing, evaluated via stress-ng and Geekbench (multi-core score of 15,345.0), falls within the average band for 48-vCPU machines. Without hardware acceleration, large-scale model inference scales poorly, reflected in 70B parameter text generation yielding 2.41 tokens/sec.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the E48bs_v5 maximizes value when deployed for memory-dense and I/O-intensive workloads where local ephemeral storage is not required. The primary tradeoff is the total reliance on networked block storage for data persistence. This profile makes the instance well suited for large relational databases, in-memory caches, enterprise ERP systems, and high-concurrency transactional database backends.
description: Microsoft Azure E48bs_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Sliced into 48 vCPUs from 24 physical cores, it offers 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The server lacks integrated local disks and GPUs, depending entirely on remote block storage systems configured for high I/O throughput. Benchmark evaluations show strong results in uncached memory bandwidth, PassMark database operations, and cryptographic processing, while general CPU compute sits within the expected average for this resource size. CPU-only large language model inference shows limited viability on 70B models, reinforcing that the hardware is tailored for memory-bound tasks. The E48bs_v5 is effectively positioned for memory-intensive database engines, distributed caching clusters, and enterprise analytics workloads requiring substantial RAM allocations alongside consistent storage throughput.
